instruction: Design §2.1. In `taskTable`, immediately after the anchor line `dueDate: timestamp("due_date", { mode: "date" }),` (which sits just before `createdAt`), add one column: `estimatedHours: integer("estimated_hours"),`. `integer` is already imported in this file — do not add an import. The column MUST be nullable with NO `.default(0)` and NO `.notNull()`: `null` means "not estimated" and is semantically distinct from `0` ("estimated at nothing", a legal value per DR-3). A default would make every pre-existing task claim an estimate it never received. Add NO index: DR-1 computes the rollup client-side, so the column is never a WHERE/ORDER BY target. Do not touch the table's five existing indexes or the `task_project_number_unique` constraint. Do not modify any other table. Do not hand-write any migration SQL — the migration is generated separately by `pnpm --filter @kaneo/api db:generate`.

Do not regenerate or edit `apps/docs/openapi.json` (it is ~11 route-groups stale and regenerating produces ~1,481 insertions of unrelated churn). Change nothing else in this file.

instruction: Design §4.1-§4.3. (1) At module scope immediately after the `VALID_PRIORITIES` declaration, insert `const ESTIMATED_HOURS_MAX = 1000;` and a single shared `estimatedHoursValidator` = `v.optional(v.nullable(v.pipe(v.number(), v.integer(...), v.minValue(0, ...), v.maxValue(ESTIMATED_HOURS_MAX, ...))))` with the messages from the design. Keep the DR-3/DR-5 comment: bounded at the validator so an out-of-range value is a 400, never a PostgreSQL "integer out of range" 500; `optional` = omitted, `nullable` = explicitly cleared. ONE constant used by both bodies so create and update cannot diverge. (2) Create route `POST /:projectId`: in its `validator("json", ...)` object add `estimatedHours: estimatedHoursValidator,` after `userId: v.optional(v.string()),`; add `estimatedHours` to the handler destructure of `c.req.valid("json")` and pass `estimatedHours,` into the `createTask({...})` call. (3) Update route `PUT /:id`: same validator addition after its `userId` line; add `estimatedHours` to the handler destructure and append `estimatedHours` as the LAST positional argument to `updateTask(...)`, after `currentUserId`. Do not change middleware chains or `describeRoute` blocks. The handler must not decide preserve-vs-clear — it forwards `undefined` through untouched.

Create route passes `estimatedHours` into `createTask({...})`; update route passes it as the last positional arg to `updateTask(...)`
Middleware chains, permission guards, and `describeRoute` metadata are unchanged
Handler contains no `||` coercion or preserve/clear branching for this field

instruction: Design §4.4. (1) Add `estimatedHours` to the destructured parameter object of `createTask` and add `estimatedHours?: number | null;` to its inline parameter type. (2) Inside `tx.insert(taskTable).values({ ... })`, anchor on `dueDate: dueDate || null,` and add directly after it: `estimatedHours: estimatedHours ?? null,`. TRAP: use `??`, NEVER `||`. `0 || null` evaluates to `null`, which would silently discard a legitimate zero-hour estimate — and `0` is a real, DR-3-permitted estimate distinct from `null` ("not estimated"). Leave the neighbouring `startDate`/`dueDate` `|| null` lines exactly as they are; changing date semantics is out of scope. Nothing else changes: the `returning()` row now carries `estimatedHours`, so the `task.created` event payload (`{ ...createdTask, ... }`) and the HTTP response both pick it up with no further edit.

instruction: Design §4.5 — the DR-5 implementation, the highest-risk hunk in the run. (1) Append `estimatedHours?: number | null,` as the LAST positional parameter, after `currentUserId?: string,`, so no existing call site breaks. Semantics: `undefined` = omitted (preserve), `null` = clear, number = set. (2) Replace the single `const [updatedTask] = await db.update(taskTable).set({ ... })` statement with: build `const updateValues: Partial<typeof taskTable.$inferInsert> = { title, status, columnId: column?.id ?? null, startDate: startDate || null, dueDate: dueDate || null, projectId, description, priority, position, userId: userId || null };` then `if (estimatedHours !== undefined) { updateValues.estimatedHours = estimatedHours; }` then `.set(updateValues)`. Keep the DR-5 comment explaining that full-PUT callers (drag-and-drop, archive-all, MCP, draft promotion) must not erase the estimate. TRAP: do NOT write `estimatedHours || null` or `?? null` — the `x || null` shape on the startDate/dueDate lines is exactly the priority-empty-string bug in a new field, and `0 || null` would destroy a valid zero estimate. Leave those two date lines byte-identical. Everything after the update statement — 404/500 guards, `task.status_changed` / `task-relation.refresh` / `task.updated` events, `deleteOrphanedAssets` — is unchanged. This field publishes no new event.

instruction: Design §5 — `buildFullTaskUpdateBody` (a read-modify-write reconstructing a full PUT body from `existing` + `patch`). (1) Widen the return type annotation to `Record<string, string | number | null | undefined>` so an explicit clear is representable. (2) Immediately after the two `formatOptionalIso` lines for `startDate`/`dueDate`, insert: `const estimatedHoursRaw = patch.estimatedHours !== undefined ? patch.estimatedHours : existing.estimatedHours;` then `const estimatedHours = estimatedHoursRaw === null ? null : typeof estimatedHoursRaw === "number" ? estimatedHoursRaw : undefined;`. Note the `!== undefined` check and the `typeof === "number"` guard — never `||`, because `0` is a real estimate that must survive. (3) Widen the `const body: Record<string, string | number | undefined> = {...}` declaration to include `null`, and add `if (estimatedHours !== undefined) body.estimatedHours = estimatedHours;` alongside the existing trailing conditional assignments for `startDate`, `dueDate`, `userId`, before `return body;`. Behaviour: patch omits → existing value forwarded; explicit `null` → clears; number → sets; out-of-range → 400 from the §4.1 validator, not coerced here; malformed `existing` degrades to omission (a DR-5 no-op), never to an erase. Do NOT touch `packages/mcp` — it is off-limits this run; if its schemas need the field, that is a recorded follow-up only.

instruction: Design §4.2. Do not change any other type in the file and do not remove the optionality.

instruction: Design §4.3b — the most failure-prone hunk in Part 2. In the `json` body, anchor between `dueDate: task.dueDate?.toString(),` and `position: task.position ?? 0,` and insert: `...(task.estimatedHours === undefined ? {} : { estimatedHours: task.estimatedHours }),` with the DR-5 comment. Semantics: `undefined` (a task read from a cache entry predating the field, e.g. a drag-and-drop payload) omits the key so the stored value is PRESERVED; explicit `null` clears; a number sets. TRAP: `?? null` is WRONG here — it would silently clear the estimate on every drag-and-drop and every column-header archive-all, both of which hand this fetcher a `Task` straight out of the board cache. Equally, never use `||`, which would also destroy a legitimate `0`. This omit branch is the guarantee; do not "simplify" it. Leave the rest of the fixed body (`userId`, `title`, `description`, `status`, `priority`, `startDate`, `dueDate`, `position`, `projectId`) exactly as it is.

Change nothing else.

instruction: Design §4.5, new file — the single place the DR-2/DR-3 parse lives so the create modal and the sidebar popover cannot drift. Export `parseEstimatedHours(raw: string): number | null | undefined`: trim; `""` → `null` (not estimated); fail `/^\d+$/` → `undefined`; otherwise `Number(trimmed)` and return it only when `Number.isInteger(value) && value >= 0 && value <= 1000`, else `undefined`. Document that `undefined` means invalid input and callers MUST NOT write it. Export `EstimatedHoursInput({ value, onCommit }: { value: number | null; onCommit: (next: number | null) => void })`: `useTranslation`, local `raw` state seeded `value === null ? "" : String(value)` (note: `0` seeds as `"0"`, never `""`), `const parsed = parseEstimatedHours(raw)`. Render an `Input` (`type="number"`, `min={0}`, `max={1000}`, `step={1}`, `inputMode="numeric"`, placeholder `t("tasks:popover.estimatedHours.placeholder")`) committing on blur and on Enter only when `parsed !== undefined` (never a truthiness check — `0` and `null` are valid commits). When `value !== null`, render a ghost `Button` with an `X` icon and `t("tasks:popover.estimatedHours.clear")` calling `onCommit(null)`. Client parsing is convenience only; DR-3 is authoritative at the Valibot validator, which returns 400.
acceptance: `parseEstimatedHours` returns `null` for empty/whitespace, the number for `"0"`/`"8"`/`"1000"`, and `undefined` for `"8.5"`, `"-1"`, `"1001"`, `"abc"`
Commit guards use `parsed !== undefined`, never truthiness, so `0` commits
The input seeds from `value` such that `0` renders as `"0"` and only `null` renders empty
The clear button renders only when `value !== null` and calls `onCommit(null)`
All user-facing strings come from static i18n keys via `useTranslation`

instruction: Design §4.5, new file — mirror `apps/web/src/components/task/task-due-date-popover.tsx` structurally (popover + permission gate + toast), including its bare-children escape. Default-export `TaskEstimatedHoursPopover({ task, children }: { task: Task; children: React.ReactNode })`. Use `useTranslation`, `useState` for `open`, `const { mutateAsync: updateTask } = useUpdateTask()`, and `const { canUpdateTasks } = useWorkspacePermission()`. `handleCommit(next: number | null)` awaits `updateTask({ ...task, estimatedHours: next })` — spread the WHOLE cached task, because the full-PUT fetcher reads eight other fields off it and narrowing would drop them — then `toast.success(t("tasks:popover.estimatedHours.updateSuccess"))` and `setOpen(false)`; on error `toast.error(error instanceof Error ? error.message : t("tasks:popover.estimatedHours.updateError"))`. Before rendering the popover, `if (!canUpdateTasks()) return <>{children}</>;`. Render `Popover`/`PopoverTrigger asChild`/`PopoverContent className="p-0 w-56" align="start"` wrapping `<EstimatedHoursInput value={task.estimatedHours ?? null} onCommit={handleCommit} />`. `?? null` is correct at this boundary only (display seed); do not use `||`, which would turn a stored `0` into `null`. Add no new fetcher, hook, or endpoint — DR-4 row 3b rejects them.

The input is seeded with `task.estimatedHours ?? null` (not `||`), so `0` seeds as `0`
No new fetcher, mutation hook, or API endpoint is introduced

instruction: Design §4.6 — six hunks in one file. (1) State: after the `dueDate` state (~line 190) add `const [estimatedHours, setEstimatedHours] = useState<number | null>(null);`. (2) Reset: add `setEstimatedHours(null);` at the `setPriority("no-priority")` line in the close reset (~249) AND in the post-submit reset (~441) — BOTH; `createMore` keeps the modal mounted, so a missed reset leaks the previous task's estimate. (4) Draft creation (~line 351, after `status: draftStatus,`): `...(estimatedHours === null ? {} : { estimatedHours }),`. instruction: Design §10.1, DR-6 — three hunks. Hunk A: change the lucide import to `import { Archive, Clock, Plus } from "lucide-react";`. Hunk B: after `handleConfirmArchive` and before `return (`, derive `estimatedTasks = column.tasks.filter((task) => typeof task.estimatedHours === "number")`; `estimatedTotal = estimatedTasks.reduce((sum, task) => sum + (task.estimatedHours as number), 0)`; `estimateState` = `"none"` when `estimatedTasks.length === 0`, `"all"` when it equals `column.tasks.length`, else `"partial"`; `estimateArgs = { hours: estimatedTotal, done: estimatedTasks.length, total: column.tasks.length }`; and `estimateLabel`/`estimateText` from `tasks:kanban.estimate.{state}` and `.{state}Short` (the `none` cases take no args). Do NOT modify `handleConfirmArchive` (its `{ ...task, status: "archived" }` spread already preserves the estimate) and do not touch `column-dropzone.tsx` — the pill is display-only and must not affect drag/drop.

instruction: Design §12, the one permitted new integration file. Follow the existing `tests/api-integration/` helper and workspace-context conventions. Cover: T-1 (AC-1) POST `/api/task/tasks/:projectId` with `estimatedHours: 8` → 200, body echoes `8`, DB row is `8`; a second POST omitting the field → row is `null`. T-2 (AC-2) PUT sets `12`, then a full PUT with the complete task body MINUS `estimatedHours` → row is still `12`, NOT `null` (the DR-5 preserve-on-omit guarantee, shaped like a drag-and-drop update); also assert an explicit `null` clears. T-3 (AC-3) `-1`, `1001`, `2.5`, `"8"` on BOTH create and update → 400, and re-read the seeded row to prove no DB write occurred. T-4 (AC-4, AC-8) GET `/api/task/tasks/:projectId` — the response is wrapped `{ data, pagination }` with columns at `body.data.columns`; assert the sorted `Object.keys()` of a returned task CONTAINS `estimatedHours` (this is what catches a missing `taskSelection` entry, which `pnpm typecheck` cannot). T-5 (AC-5) single-task read returns `estimatedHours`, using the workspace context the existing helpers supply — calling `/api/task/:projectId` bare 400s with "Workspace ID could not be determined", which is the board-path mistake, not a bug. T-6 (AC-7) seed one column with `[8, null, 0, 4]`; assert sum-of-non-null `=== 12` and estimated-count `=== 3` (the `0` counts as estimated). T-7 (AC-10) rows inserted without the field read back `null`. T-8 (AC-12) a non-member gets 403 from the existing `requireWorkspacePermission` — no new guard, `packages/permissions` untouched.
acceptance: T-2 asserts a full PUT omitting `estimatedHours` leaves the stored value intact, and that explicit `null` clears it
T-4 asserts against the real `body.data.columns[].tasks[]` payload keys, not a typed fixture
T-3 asserts 400 for `-1`, `1001`, `2.5`, `"8"` on both create and update and re-reads the row to prove no write
T-6 treats `0` as estimated: sum `12`, estimated count `3` for `[8, null, 0, 4]`
Tests run against the integration harness's own database and create no new permission or guard code

instruction: Design §12 T-9 (AC-3). New file; `tests/api/task/` is currently empty, so establish the directory. Table-driven Valibot unit test over the create and update request schemas from `apps/api/src/task/index.ts` (the shared `estimatedHoursValidator` per §4.1 — assert both bodies behave identically, since one constant serves both). ACCEPT: `0`, `1`, `1000`, `undefined` (omitted), `null` (explicit clear). REJECT: `-1`, `1001`, `0.5`, `"8"` (string), `NaN`, `Infinity`. Assert acceptance/rejection via the Valibot parse result, and assert that a successful parse of an omitted field yields `undefined` (not `null` and not `0`) — that distinction is the DR-5 preserve-on-omit contract. Explicitly cover `0` as ACCEPTED and distinct from `null`: `0` is a real estimate ("estimated at nothing") and any truthiness-based implementation would fail this case. Use the repo's existing `tests/api/` test-runner idiom and imports; do not spin up a database or HTTP server.
acceptance: Table-driven cases cover accept `0`/`1`/`1000`/`undefined`/`null` and reject `-1`/`1001`/`0.5`/`"8"`/`NaN`/`Infinity`
Both the create and the update body schemas are exercised with the same table
An omitted field parses to `undefined`, asserted distinctly from `null`
The test needs no database or running server

instruction: Design §12 T-10 (AC-9). New unit test over `buildFullTaskUpdateBody` from `apps/api/src/mcp/tools.ts` (the MCP read-modify-write). Assert: (a) a patch that OMITS `estimatedHours` produces a body whose `estimatedHours` equals the existing task's value — the preserve path; (b) a patch with explicit `null` produces `estimatedHours: null` — the clear path; (c) a patch with `0` produces `estimatedHours: 0` and the key IS present — this is the guard against an `||` regression, since `0 || existing` would silently substitute the old value; (d) an `existing` whose `estimatedHours` is `undefined` or non-numeric with an omitting patch produces a body with NO `estimatedHours` key at all, which DR-5 makes a harmless no-op rather than an erase. Use plain object fixtures for `existing` and `patch`; no database, no HTTP server, no MCP transport. Follow the repo's existing `tests/api/` test-runner idiom.
acceptance: Omitting patch forwards the existing value; explicit `null` emits `null`
A patch of `0` emits `estimatedHours: 0` with the key present
A malformed/absent `existing` value with an omitting patch emits no `estimatedHours` key
Test uses plain fixtures with no database, server, or MCP transport

instruction: Design §12 T-11 (AC-6) and T-6b (AC-2, web side). New component test following the repo's existing web component-test idiom (note: these tests mock `react-i18next` so `t` echoes the key — assert on `data-estimate-state` and the accessible name/key rather than on resolved English prose; plural correctness is proved separately in the i18n test). T-11: three column fixtures — none estimated, mixed, all estimated. For each, find the rollup via `getByLabelText` (it is `role="img"` with `aria-label`), assert `data-estimate-state` is `none` / `partial` / `all` respectively, and assert the visible text differs across the three. Fourth assertion: the count pill still renders `column.tasks.length` unchanged. Fifth assertion: a `[0, null]` column reports state `partial` with a total of `0` hours — the `0` counts as estimated and must not be filtered out. T-6b: mock `useUpdateTask`, click the archive button, confirm in the modal, and assert EVERY `updateTask` call argument carries the task's original `estimatedHours` — proving archive-all preserves the estimate through the full-PUT fetcher. Do not import or exercise `column-dropzone.tsx`.
acceptance: Three fixtures assert `data-estimate-state` of `none`, `partial`, `all` via `getByLabelText`
A `[0, null]` column asserts state `partial` and total `0`, proving `0` is counted as estimated
The count pill assertion confirms `column.tasks.length` still renders
T-6b asserts every `updateTask` call from archive-all carries the original `estimatedHours`
No assertion depends on resolved English strings from the mocked `t`

instruction: Design §12 T-12 (AC-1, AC-11). This file EXISTS — extend it, preserving every existing test and its setup/mocks unchanged. Add coverage that (a) the estimated-hours trigger renders in the modal when create permission is granted (locate it by its i18n key, since `react-i18next` is mocked and `t` echoes keys), and (b) submitting WITHOUT touching the field produces a create payload with NO `estimatedHours` key at all — assert on the mocked create mutation's argument via `Object.keys()` or an `in` check, not on a `=== undefined` comparison, since the point is key absence per §4.6 hunk 5's plain-create branch. If the existing mocks make it practical, also assert that setting a value of `0` submits `estimatedHours: 0` rather than omitting it — `0` is a real estimate and `=== null` is the only correct emptiness test. instruction: Design §12 T-13. New test over `parseEstimatedHours` exported from `apps/web/src/components/task/estimated-hours-input.tsx`. Table-driven: `""` → `null`; whitespace-only → `null`; `"0"` → `0`; `"8"` → `8`; `"1000"` → `1000`; and `"8.5"`, `"-1"`, `"1001"`, `"abc"` → `undefined` (invalid). Assert the three-way distinction explicitly: `null` (cleared / not estimated), a number (set), and `undefined` (invalid, must never be written by a caller) are three different outcomes — use strict equality and, for the `null` vs `undefined` cases, assertions that distinguish them rather than a loose falsy check. Critically, assert `parseEstimatedHours("0")` returns the number `0` and NOT `null`/`undefined`, since `0` is a real DR-3-permitted estimate. Follow the repo's existing web unit-test idiom; the file may test the pure function alone and need not render the component.
acceptance: `"0"` asserts strictly to the number `0`
`null` and `undefined` outcomes are distinguished by strict assertions, not falsy checks
The test imports the exported `parseEstimatedHours` and passes without a DOM render if none is needed

instruction: Design §12 T-14 (AC-11, plural proof). Component tests in this repo mock `react-i18next` so `t` merely echoes the key — `t("x", { count: 2 })` returns the literal `"x"`, which makes plural bugs invisible. This test therefore initialises a REAL i18next instance from `i18n/en-US.json` (do not mock `react-i18next` here) and proves resolution. Assert: `tasks:properties.estimatedHours` with `count: 1` → `"1 hour"`, `count: 2` → `"2 hours"`, `count: 0` → `"0 hours"` (English plural rules make 0 plural; this also proves the `_one`/`_other` no-base-key form resolves). Assert the rollup labels `tasks:kanban.estimate.partial` / `partialShort` / `all` / `allShort` resolve with `{{hours}}`, `{{done}}`, `{{total}}` substituted, and that no resolved string contains a stray `{{` or `}}`. Assert `tasks:kanban.estimate.none` and `noneShort` resolve to non-empty strings. Do NOT pass `count` to any rollup label — `count` is reserved by i18next for plural selection and would hijack resolution.
acceptance: A real i18next instance loads `i18n/en-US.json`; `react-i18next` is not mocked in this file
`estimatedHours` resolves to `"1 hour"` for count 1 and `"2 hours"` / `"0 hours"` for counts 2 and 0
Rollup labels resolve with hours/done/total substituted and contain no residual `{{`
No rollup assertion passes a `count` option
